title: Semester and Playlist
premise: Ada Galloway, seventeen, holds her family together with night-shift leftovers and an ironclad rule: never make waves. But when her senior English teacher assigns a college essay answering 'What truth have you been keeping?', Ada writes about the chemistry lab her younger brother was burned in—and the maintenance report the school board quietly shredded. Her essay wins a regional prize and drags the buried incident into daylight, costing her the scholarship she was counting on. With her mother's job threatened and her siblings watching, Ada must decide whether loyalty to family means silence or exposure, ultimately testifying before the board and trading her invisible, 'fine' life for a messier, truer inheritance: the courage her late grandmother left in a box of unsent letters.
about_author: Odile Vane is a former night-shift nurse who wrote her first novel on break-room napkins while raising three younger brothers. She lives in a rust-belt town much like the one in this book, where she teaches community writing workshops for teens.

chapters.title: Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A chaotic morning—burnt toast, a missing bus pass, seven-year-old Milo's scraped knee—establishes Ada's role as surrogate parent while Mom works nights at the hospital. The emotional beat: competent exhaustion, and Ada's practiced smile that convinces everyone, including herself, that everything is fine.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In Mr. Okonkwo's English class, the college essay prompt 'What truth have you been keeping?' lands on Ada's desk like a dare. She writes a safe, forgettable answer about learning responsibility. Emotional beat: a flicker of something unquiet when she glances at the scar on Milo's hand.

chapters.title: Playlist for a Long Night
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, interwoven with texts from her best friend Priya. Ada builds the playlist she plays while her siblings do homework—the family's nightly ritual. Emotional beat: warmth, but also the realization that music is the only place she lets herself feel anything.

chapters.title: What Milo Remembers
chapters.summary: Milo's POV, a short chapter in a child's voice. Milo describes the day of the lab fire in fragments: the smell, the teacher's panic, a man in a coverall taking away a clipboard. Emotional beat: innocent confusion that quietly contradicts the official story Ada was told.

chapters.title: The Draft She Doesn't Submit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At 2 a.m., Ada writes the real essay—the fire, the shredded maintenance report her grandmother once mentioned. She saves it, tells herself she'll delete it. Emotional beat: terror and relief in the same breath, the first crack in her silence.

chapters.title: Grandma Ruth's Box
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cleaning the attic, Ada finds her late grandmother's box: unsent letters to the school board, a copy of a 2019 inspection report flagging the lab's fume hood. Emotional beat: grief braided with inheritance—Ruth fought this fight alone and lost.

chapters.title: Submission Error
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, helping Ada with scholarship applications, accidentally submits the wrong essay file—the true one—to the regional contest. Emotional beat: Priya's guilt and her conviction that the accident was a mercy; Ada's fury masks fear.

chapters.title: Shortlisted
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The essay is shortlisted; a local reporter emails asking to interview her. Mom, home at dawn, reads it and goes very quiet. Emotional beat: the family's fragile stability suddenly balanced on a piece of paper.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Shift
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. A chapter inside Mom's exhausting double shifts, her fear that the school board—her employer's biggest donor—will retaliate, her memory of signing a settlement she never understood. Emotional beat: a mother's love expressed as 'don't rock the boat.'

chapters.title: The Interview
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The reporter, Dana Reyes, is kind and relentless. Ada gives careful half-answers but mentions the inspection report. Emotional beat: the strange power of being believed for the first time.

chapters.title: Front Page, Small Town
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in brief vignettes: classmates, teachers, Milo's proud confusion, Mom's missed calls. Emotional beat: Ada becomes visible whether she wants to be or not; the word 'whistleblower' attaches itself to a girl who just wanted a scholarship.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The school board chair, Mr. Calloway, meets Ada privately: a full-ride scholarship, a public 'misunderstanding' retraction, in exchange for her silence. He invokes her family's needs. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as kindness; Ada sees her mother's exhaustion in his argument.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Weighed
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya argues truth matters more; Ada argues survival matters more; their friendship fractures. Emotional beat: the painful discovery that loyalty and truth are not automatically the same thing.

chapters.title: What the Settlement Bought
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Mom finally tells Ada the whole story: the settlement money that fixed the roof, the NDA she signed, the shame she's carried. Emotional beat: mother and daughter, both keepers of secrets, finally in the same room honestly.

chapters.title: Milo's Question
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Milo asks Ada directly: 'Was it my fault?' Ada realizes the buried report isn't abstract—it's the reason her brother flinches at Bunsen burners. Emotional beat: protective rage crystallizes into resolve.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The board meets in nine days; the scholarship acceptance is due in five. Dana confirms a second family from 2019 is willing to speak—if Ada goes first. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist; every choice costs something.

chapters.title: The Retraction Draft
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada writes the retraction Calloway demanded, then reads her grandmother's unsent letters aloud to her siblings. Emotional beat: Ruth's voice across time—'They counted on us being tired'—and Ada deciding tired is not the same as silent.

chapters.title: Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, high tension. Ada testifies, reads the 2019 inspection report into the record, and is followed by the second family. Calloway stonewalls; a board member defects. Emotional beat: terror transforming into voice; the room shifts.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The story breaks wide; Calloway resigns; the district orders lab inspections. But the scholarship is gone and Mom's hours are cut. Emotional beat: victory that feels like loss; Priya and Ada reconcile over what loyalty actually means.

chapters.title: The Essay That Wins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A state journalism scholarship—awarded for the essay itself—arrives, smaller than the lost one but hers, earned by truth. Emotional beat: quiet vindication; Ada learns inheritance isn't money, it's what you refuse to bury.

chapters.title: Playlist for a New Morning
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A mirror of chapter three: the same chaotic morning, but Ada plays a different first song, and Milo asks to add one. Emotional beat: the family ritual transformed—still tired, still messy, no longer invisible.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing. Ada submits her final college application, essay question answered honestly, and visits Ruth's grave to report the news. Emotional beat: resolution and forward motion—Ada graduates from keeping everyone safe to keeping everyone honest, including herself.
